Old audio lengths in Supabase are wrong. page_audio.audio_duration_seconds is computed as bytes / (44100 x 2 x 2), but the WAV is 24 kHz mono 16-bit, so every stored value is about 3.7x too short (b1 p5: stored 22 s, real 80 s). This page uses real lengths read from the WAV headers.
Two old cached pages (b2 p12, b3 p10) hold the whole model reply as a raw JSON string inside body, so the old TTS was sent the JSON keys, quotes and the footer text.

The old pipeline speaks the stored header before the body. On these pages the header is often a running header plus the page number (b2 p9 '٩ مقدمة', b3 p9 'التَّسْوِيرُ … ٨'), so page numbers and book titles are read aloud, sometimes in the middle of a sentence that crosses the page edge. Worst case b2 p10 → p11: the old audio says '… إنهم يريدوننا أن' then '١١ مقدمة' then 'نؤمن به'. The new pipeline merges this into one segment. MAX_TEXT_LENGTH is 4800 in this env, so no old page was truncated before TTS.

Old text dropped content the new extraction kept. On b1 p5 the old body leaves out 'ومشكلات المسلمين يمكن أن تحل' and 'والاجتراء على دخول الساحة الفكرية', and misreads لبسوا as ليسوا and التبسيط as التيسيط. The scan confirms the new text. Body text otherwise agrees within 0–2% characters on 8 of 12 pages (diacritics and punctuation stripped).

New extraction defect: on b3 p9 gemini-3.8-flash wrote 'أن أserver ثمار' where the page prints 'أن أجتني ثمار'. A Latin token was decoded inside an Arabic word, at temperature 0. A cheap guard (Latin letters glued to Arabic letters inside one word) would catch it.

New extraction also normalises some typography: the superscript alef in printed 'علىٰ' and 'إلىٰ' is dropped (b3), and the running header 'التَّسوير' came back as 'التَّصوير'. The header is not spoken, so the second does not reach audio.

Roles look right on all 12 pages: page numbers in three digit styles (– ۹ –, ٩, ١٠), the www.Quranonlinelibrary.com watermark and the publisher line tagged footer, running headers, and footnotes split per note. Footnote markers such as (١) were removed from body text and listed separately.
MINIMAL thinking is rejected by gemini-3.8-flash (400 'not supported for this model'), so the run used LOW. LOW reported 0 thinking tokens on every page.

Cross-page merges: 5 boundaries were merged, and in every case the model flag, the punctuation heuristic and the next page's starts_mid_sentence flag agreed. The 4 unmerged boundaries all end with terminal punctuation. No disagreements to review.

Book 3 is not a voice-for-voice comparison: its old audio is the 'Islamic Book Reader' persona (Algieba plus a dramatic/enthusiastic style prompt). The new audio is plain Algieba with no style. Zephyr audio exists for only 3 consecutive pages of that book (6–8), so a 4-page Zephyr window was not possible.

The Gemini key is on the FREE tier. gemini-3.8-flash-tts stopped after 10 calls with quota GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel-FreeTier (10). gemini-3.8-flash also returned 429/503 under 4 parallel calls, so extraction runs one page at a time. Dollar figures here are list-price values; nothing was billed. Production at any volume needs a paid tier, and whole-book pre-generation would suit the Batch API.

New TTS measured 22.9 audio tokens per second (the doc assumes 25), so $0.75 per audio hour against the $0.81 list estimate. Extraction at LOW thinking cost $0.0047 per page; the old pipeline estimate is $0.0045, because 3.8 Flash has higher per-token rates even with zero thinking tokens. These are on a 12-page sample.
